newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening mixed on economic news.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening mixed on economic news.

text.p: * Toronto stocks are expected to open mixed on slightly better than expected U.S. economic news, but under pressure from profit-taking related to Wednesday's rally to a new record.

Toronto stocks were expected to open mixed on Thursday with the possibility of heading weaker or stronger on the day depending on which of the competing forces can win the minds of investors, traders said.

They said a slightly better than expected report on U.S. second quarter gross domestic product could buoy the market, while profit-taking on the back of Wednesday's record high rally will put a drag on any gains.
"I still think it may open lower but it has now a 50/50 chance of going up on the day, because the numbers are a little better than expected," one trader said.

The U.S. reported that second quarter GDP rose 2.2 percent compared to a revised first quarter rise of 4.9 percent, but GDP deflator rose only 1.4 percent in the second quarter compared to 2.4 percent in the first.
"The economy grew a little more than people expected and with the deflator down that's sort of positive that there is no inflation lying around I guess," the trader said.
On Wednesday, the Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 composite index soared 49.40 points to a record high finish at 6850.57, its third straight record this week.
Toronto's early trading volume was heavier than in recent sessions, totalling about 130 million shares worth C$1.8 billion.
Advancing stocks clobbered declines 611 to 419 with 266 issues unchanged.
